biodiversity_overview.text: 3,654 GBIF occurrence records for 27 tracked species are attributed to Tripura, spanning 2009-2026.
3,622 of these records (99.1%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 12, Testudines 5, Magnoliopsida 4, Mammalia 4, Actinopterygii 2.

threatened_species.text: 7 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
1 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Asian Elephant (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Pied Starling (1,481), Indian Cuckoo (1,202), Indian Pond-heron (358), Indian White-eye (346), Indian Spotted Eagle (108).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 12 in 2016 to 31 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 4.97% of Tripura's area (4 areas intersect the state).
3.8% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (136 of 3,622); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Narrow-headed Softshell Turtle (0.54), Peacock Soft-shelled Turtle (0.50), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Roofed Turtle (0.36), Indian Gooseberry (0.35).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Tripura (equal-weight reference): cell near 23.625N 91.125E (overall rank 5, median rank across weightings 11); cell near 24.375N 91.875E (overall rank 275, median rank across weightings 276); cell near 22.875N 91.125E (overall rank 288, median rank across weightings 281).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 7,398 km2 (60.67% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

1,588.0 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (21.46% of the 2000 extent; 14.42% in 2015-2024, rank 1 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2017 (157.63 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 1.67% of land and population density is 472.8 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
22% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
